$comment: Declarative readiness evidence for the Manna progress report.
Why a hand-maintained file rather than inference: the statuses below are
CLAIMS, and a claim needs named evidence and a reviewer. Deriving them
automatically would mean guessing — and a dashboard that guesses
'VERIFIED' is worse than no dashboard, because it manufactures exactly
the false confidence the audit record exists to prevent.
So every entry carries an `evidence` string, and changing a status is a
reviewable diff in a pull request. Anything not actually checked is
NOT RUN or BLOCKED, never VERIFIED.
Permitted status values: VERIFIED, PARTIAL, BLOCKED, NOT RUN,
NOT APPLICABLE. No percentages — there is no defined denominator, so a
verifiedAgainstCommit: BASELINE: master at 403acf1, deployed to Vercel Production and CONFIRMED serving (deployment 7344985889 state success; owner-reported dpl_BZgDHuZxjbG2NHgg12b218eoQT3q READY on alias carloscab74.vercel.app). All four required checks green and ENFORCED by ruleset 25851827. NOT YET ON MASTER — attributable to two stacked unmerged branches and not to the baseline above: the 66 files / 943 tests figure, and the VERIFIED status of the 'Durable volume control on the three P2P money paths (send, request-accept, split-pay)' row. That row was named 'every money path' until review of PR #75 pointed out that its own evidence recorded the transfer rail holding no claim; it is now scoped to what it verifies, and the rail is a separate row at NOT RUN. PR #74 (branch docs/sprint1-owner-confirmations, head 04bb94e) adds the velocity gate to paySplitPortion(); PR #75 (branch claude/cool-cerf-ErxD3), measured at commit f520e22 — its head at the time of measurement, named that way because an earlier revision of this field and of CURRENT_STATUS.md both asserted a commit WAS the head and were falsified by the next push; which targets #74's branch rather than master so #74's known check-then-record defect is never deployed alone, and replaces check-then-record with atomic admission on all three money paths (decision 0008). Both become baseline facts when BOTH branches merge and not before; they are named here rather than left to read as master's state, because this field otherwise says rows describe master unless they name a PR. Every other row describes master.

operational.name: Redis-backed rate limiting in production
operational.evidence: CONFIGURATION CONFIRMED, OPERATION NOT VERIFIED. The owner reports REDIS_URL is set for production (2026-10-20, name only; no value requested or held by this session). That is not the same claim as "limits are shared": lib/rate-limit.ts falls back to in-process counters on any Redis client or command failure. The RAW EXCEPTION is deliberately not logged because it can embed the credential-bearing URL; a degradation line naming the stage and a cumulative count is emitted to stderr, so a signal exists but carries no connection detail. The degradation itself IS caller-visible — allowed and remaining change, and a caller spreading requests across instances can exceed the nominal limit; what is missing is an explicit backend-failure signal. A failure no longer latches: it sets redisDownUntil, which suppresses Redis attempts for a 30s cooldown and then retries, so an instance recovers on its own instead of counting in-process until it recycles. rateLimitBackendHealth() reports activeBackend, cooldown state and the cumulative degradation count, with no credential in it. (An earlier version of this row described the old permanent redisUnavailable latch; that variable no longer exists.) Operational proof needs POST /api/admin/operations/redis-rate-limit run against production with an authenticated admin session holding the exceptions:manage permission — SuperAdmin or OperationsAdmin; a lesser admin role gets 403, which is easy to misread as Redis being down. That route performs an isolated set/get/delete and is already implemented and audited. ONE POST PROVES ONLY THE INSTANCE THAT SERVED IT: the backend state and the in-process counters are module-level in lib/rate-limit.ts, therefore per serverless instance, so another live instance can still be counting in-process while this one answers pass. Serverless instances cannot be addressed individually, so repeated POSTs give sampling confidence rather than coverage; VERIFIED requires evidence covering every live instance, or equivalent deployment-wide evidence, which in practice means monitoring the degradation signal rather than an operator running the route by hand. Nothing external scrapes that signal yet. Row therefore stays PARTIAL on a passing POST. POLICY NOW DECIDED (2026-10-26): the owner ACCEPTED keeping all three money buckets fail-open on Redis loss (docs/decisions/0007, status Accepted), with a fail-closed requirement in the other direction — if velocity_checks cannot be evaluated atomically, the money path must refuse. SUPERSEDED 2026-11-07 BY DECISION 0008, and this paragraph is corrected rather than deleted because it was true when written: it read that the requirement 'holds today only incidentally — checkVelocityLimit has no try/catch and no caller wraps it' and that only money:split-pay had a test pinning it. admitVelocity() now implements it explicitly on all three balance-moving paths — it has no try/catch, no caller wraps it, and a refusal THROWS rather than returning, so a catch added 'to be resilient' would both invert the requirement and swallow VelocityLimitError, turning a refusal into an admission. split-pay-velocity.test.ts and velocity-admission.test.ts fail on exactly that mutation. The remaining path is the transfer rail, which consumes no budget at all — an absent control rather than an unpinned one; see its own row. A Vercel execution ceiling is now documented — Pro plan, Fluid Compute, 30,000 concurrent executions, 1,000 per 10s per region burst — so 'formally unbounded' is withdrawn at that layer, but it is an EXECUTION ceiling and not an instance count, so no exact in-process multiplier may be claimed. Do not write 30,000 and do not write 'small'.

operational.name: Durable volume control on the three P2P money paths (send, request-accept, split-pay)
operational.evidence: SCOPE, STATED FIRST BECAUSE THE PREVIOUS ROW NAME OVERSTATED IT: this row covers money:send, request-accept and money:split-pay only. It was named 'every money path' and marked VERIFIED while its own evidence recorded that the transfer rail holds no velocity claim — a true body under a name drawn too wide, so a report rendering the status without the body would have shown the rail gap as resolved. Raised in review of PR #75 and corrected here; the rail is now its own row below. RESOLVED. Two stages, both now complete. STAGE 1, 2026-10-26 (owner-authorized option A): lib/splits.ts contained ZERO velocity references, so paySplitPortion() debited the payer and credited the split creator with no durable volume control at all, and its volume never entered velocity_checks to consume any other path's budget — falsifying a premise of the ACCEPTED decision 0007. The gate was added INSIDE paySplitPortion() rather than in the route, deliberately: the amount is read from split_participants under FOR UPDATE, so the amount checked is exactly the amount about to move, and any future caller inherits the control — the control living only in routes is precisely why this path was missed. STAGE 2, 2026-11-07 (owner-authorized option B, docs/decisions/0008): the TOCTOU that stage 1 inherited is closed. Every path ran checkVelocityLimit() -> move money -> recordVelocity(): two statements on two snapshots with nothing holding the payer's rows between them, so two concurrent payments by one payer both read the pre-payment total and both were admitted (CWE-367). admitVelocity() now claims the three window rows first (row locks held to commit), verifies after, and throws VelocityLimitError on a breach — which rolls the claim back. money:send, request-accept and money:split-pay all admit inside their money transaction passing tx. Refusal throws rather than returning, so 'a refused payment consumes no budget' is control flow and not a convention a caller must remember. Two further defects closed by the same change: the post-commit velocity writes on money:send and request-accept, which returned 500 for payments that had already succeeded; and 0007's fail-closed requirement, which until now held only incidentally and was pinned on one path — it is now implemented and pinned on all three. EVIDENCE: 66 files / 943 tests, all passing on a fresh fixtured database; typecheck 0 errors; lint 0 errors / 28 pre-existing warnings; pnpm run build succeeds. MUTATION-CHECKED against real PostgreSQL: reversing admitVelocity() to read-then-write is caught by 2 cases; dropping its own-transaction wrapper by 4; dropping the tx argument in lib/splits.ts by 5, including the static caller guard and a 5s pool-deadlock timeout. lib/__tests__/velocity-admission-callers.test.ts is a static guard: no money path may call checkVelocityLimit() (one allowlisted preview site) or recordVelocity(), and every admitVelocity() call must pass an executor — because the defect was a SHAPE copied from path to path, so fixing four callers while leaving the unsafe pair exported invites the fifth to reintroduce it silently. A NEGATIVE RESULT WORTH RECORDING: the obvious concurrency test — two admissions that fit singly but not together, assert one wins — PASSED under the read-then-write mutation, because whether they interleave is up to the scheduler. It was replaced with an assertion on the LOCK (hold one transaction open, require the second to be unable to decide), which is deterministic. BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, stated because it is not purely additive: a split portion consumes the payer's velocity budget, so a payer near their ceiling on other paths can be refused a split payment previously allowed; and a payer firing concurrent payments near their ceiling now has those attempts serialized against each other and may be refused one that previously went through. Both are the intended effect. Distinct payers are unaffected — they take disjoint rows. No user is newly locked out for being unverified: the velocity tier selects new_user vs verified_user limits, it does not gate on KYC. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: the TRANSFER RAIL consumes no velocity budget anywhere. POST /api/transfers/intent runs a non-binding preview and no confirm or execute route has ever written velocity, despite that route's comment claiming it was 'recorded at confirm'. Sandbox confirm does move the platform balance, so that is a balance-moving path with no durable volume control — the same gap split-pay had, on a different rail. Out of scope for 0008 by decision, recorded as an open gap in CLAUDE.md. EXTENDED VALIDATION 2026-11-08 (0008 addendum): five uncovered behaviours from the owner's validation list are now pinned — CAD/USD budget isolation; window rollover (a previous hour out of scope hourly, still counted daily); the daily-amount and weekly-amount ceilings, neither reachable by a sequence of admissions and so neither previously tested; that reverseVelocity()'s compensating rows actually release headroom, true only because admission sums all rows in a window rather than reading the row it upserted; and 429-not-500 on money:send and request-accept, whose VelocityLimitError catch branches are new code on paths that had no route test. Deleting either route's branch fails three cases with 'expected 500 to be 429'. Pool exhaustion on those two routes is foreclosed structurally rather than behaviourally — the static caller guard requires an executor and both route tests assert it is the transaction's own tx object. ALL OF THIS IS CODE VERIFICATION, not production operational verification: nothing has run against the production database, and behaviour under Supabase's transaction pooler is unobserved. NOT YET ON MASTER: stage 1 is PR #74 (unmerged); stage 2 is PR #75 (branch claude/cool-cerf-ErxD3), stacked on #74's head 04bb94e and targeting #74's branch.

operational.name: Durable volume control on the transfer rail (add_money / cash_out)
operational.evidence: NOT IMPLEMENTED. The rail consumes no velocity budget: POST /api/transfers/intent runs a NON-BINDING preview and no confirm, execute or settlement path has ever written velocity_checks, while sandbox confirm DOES move a real platform balance via settleSandboxTransfer(). THE RELEASE PREREQUISITE IS ADDRESSED BUT UNMERGED AND UNVALIDATED. reverseVelocity() released min(amount, current window total) — a total spanning every money path — so a returned transfer freed budget money:send and money:split-pay genuinely consumed. It is deleted and replaced on branch sec/claim-bounded-velocity-release (docs/decisions/0012) by a claim ledger keyed (provider, reference) with exposure DERIVED per accounting domain. READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THAT FIX: its FIRST implementation reproduced the same cross-domain error in the opposite direction and its own tests ASSERTED it. velocity_checks has no domain column, so it is one pool holding money:send, request-accept and money:split-pay consumption together; the first version wrote negative 'compensating' rows into it. Measured: a funding release cut pure P2P volume 450->350; a WITHDRAWAL release cut it 400->250; a release with no prior charge drove usage to -300, after which the payer moved 750 against a 500 hourly ceiling — a 50% ceiling bypass. Clamping the negatives would have hidden the third case and left the first two. The model was changed instead: the module now writes to velocity_checks not at all, and exposure is a SUM over positive amounts of the reserved subset, so it cannot go negative by construction. ALSO FIXED: the release called auditLog() inside its transaction; auditLog() takes its own connection and swallows errors. Mutation restoring it TIMES OUT the six-concurrent-release test at 5s with cascading hook timeouts (the max:5 pool deadlock, hanging rather than failing), and the atomicity cases report 'resolved instead of rejecting'. The audit row also committed independently, so it outlived a rolled-back release. EVIDENCE: 67 files / 965 tests pass at 6b0ceb8; typecheck 0; lint 0 errors; build succeeds. Mutation-checked four ways — the cross-domain write is caught by 12 cases across four files, including a static guard that forbids any velocity_checks write in lib/velocity-claims.ts. THE OWNER REQUIRES INDEPENDENT VALIDATION OF THE ACCOUNTING MODEL BEFORE THAT BRANCH MERGES, and no rail may be enabled until it is verified. ARCHITECTURE: docs/decisions/0009 is ACCEPTED (Option C, architecture only, 2026-11-08) — reserve at confirm, finalize at verified settlement, release only the matching claim, idempotent reconciliation, no DB transaction held open across a provider call, separate funding and withdrawal exposure. Limits are NOT approved: 0010 (Proposed) derives them from Plaid's published ceiling, which for an unapproved Implementation Checklist — Manna's state — is $100 per transfer / $500 per day / $1,000 per month. 0011 (Proposed) carries the realized-loss design the owner chose over accepting repeated NSF returns. 0013 (Proposed) replaces 0009's sandbox step 2, WHICH WAS WRONG: it said to admit with admitVelocity(), which would have made a simulated add_money consume the payer's real P2P outbound budget.

ownerActions.action: Compare two production requests to settle header trust
ownerActions.why: Send TWO production requests and report, for each, clientIdentity().source AND whether the resolved id EQUALS the forged value that request supplied — a boolean, never the id and never the IP. Request A sends no IP headers. Request B supplies a distinctive forged value in x-real-ip, x-forwarded-for and x-vercel-forwarded-for. The source name alone does NOT answer this: if both requests select x-vercel-forwarded-for the name is identical whether the platform overwrote the forged value or passed it through, so only the equality tells you which happened. If B's id equals what B sent, the header is attacker-controlled and every limit keyed on it is per-attempt, not per-client. PR #71 documents the question; this environment cannot answer it (403 CONNECT to both api.vercel.com and the deployment host).
